thread.title: QQQ: Why Are We Still Falling? - Invesco QQQ ETF (NASDAQ:QQQ)

author: Income Generator
title: QQQ: Why Are We Still Falling? - Invesco QQQ ETF (NASDAQ:QQQ)
text:
Stock markets continue to trade under a dark cloud of bearish pressure, and the Invesco NASDAQ Trust ( QQQ ) has lost 14.77% since the ETF reached its highs in August. For many, these moves have been surprising because tech stocks have been consistent leaders in the bull market rally which followed the 2008 financial crisis. At the same time, these types of rallies may strengthen the suggestion that another "tech bubble" is in place and that what we are seeing now is a long-term top in instruments like the QQQ ETF. Of course, these are all important considerations for investors in these types of environments. But the quarterly performance results this earnings season have failed to validate the bearish concerns. As a result, it looks as though perception has moved too far away from reality. Ultimately, this suggests rallies may lie ahead for those with long exposure to QQQ.
(Source: ETF.com)
The Invesco NASDAQ Trust has an expense ratio of 0.20% and is heavily devoted to the technology sector (at 61.33% of the total holdings). The fund is well-diversified ETF with additional allocations in consumer cyclicals (21.04%) and healthcare (9.10%). This adds a protective layer of sector diversification for those holding positions in QQQ.
(Source: ETFdb.com)
Over the last few weeks, headlines in the financial news media have focused negative attention on the technology sector. Given the sector allocation present in QQQ, it is not surprising that the fund has been on the receiving end of the market's bearish momentum activity. But we are already seeing clear evidence which suggests that investors are looking to buy at these lower valuations, and this creates stronger possibilities for bullish reversals in the weeks ahead.
Over the last four weeks, the fund has benefited from inflows of $475.0 million. But the QQQ inflows seen over the last week have been far stronger (more than doubling the monthly figure at $983.9 million). As short-term inflows outpace longer-term inflows, we can see that market sentiment is starting to turn in favor of those with long positions in QQQ.
(Source: Author/TradingView)
Additional evidence supporting the bullish outlook can be found in the quarterly earnings performances of the fund's core holdings. Amazon ( AMZN ) makes up 9.96% of the total holdings in QQQ, and the stock has fallen 20.60% over the last three months. These moves have taken many investors by surprise, as AMZN has actually fallen through important psychological levels at $1,500.
These types of moves can have a substantial impact on sentiment. But the declines have not yet deterred investors ready to "buy on the dip," as we can clearly see from the QQQ fund inflows which have been present over the last week. The negative short-term outlook for AZMN fails to match the longer-term trends, as share prices still show significant YTD gains of 27.88%. The bullish performances may be difficult to remember given all of the recent volatility in share prices.
But Amazon's third quarter earnings performances remain supportive, as the company generated earnings of $5.75 per share. This nearly doubled the analyst expectation for the period ($3.14 per share) and total profits of $2.9 billion for the period. This marks an annualized growth rate of 1,032.81% when compared to the profits posted during the third quarter of 2017 ($256 million). For anyone with a rational outlook, this fails to explain or justify the recent declines in the stock.
(Source: Author/TradingView)
Another example of irrational market activity can be found with the recent market declines in Apple ( AAPL ) share prices. AAPL makes up the largest holding in QQQ, with its valuation representing 11.66% of the fund. The company's share price fell by 4.8% on Tuesday alone, and this officially puts the stock in "correction" territory. Remember, a "correction" is a market term which is used to describe an asset that has fallen more than 20% from its recent highs. AAPL hit highs of $232.07 on October 3, and these latest declines have forced share prices to near-term lows below $177 per share. This marks a decline of 23.74% as investors continue punishing negative earnings (while overlooking examples of strength in corporate profitability).
Apple should be viewed as a key example here, as the company posted earnings of $2.91 per share during the fiscal fourth quarter. This marked a massive beat on the consensus expectations ($2.78 per share), and revenues were also above analyst estimates of $61.57 billion (at $62.9 billion). Of course, Apple's most recent report was not entirely positive as it indicated weaker iPhone sales relative to the consensus estimates (46.89 million actual vs. 47.5 million expected). But the company's impressive margins offset this weaker performance, as the average sale price for each iPhone sold posted at $793. All combined, heightened operational efficiency generated strong earnings results for the quarter. But recent moves in the market failed to reflect this strength. At some stage, those disparities will become glaring and this should stoke investor optimism for those looking to buy the dips.
(Source: Author/TradingView)
Has this activity already started? It may be difficult to believe that we are currently in the early stages of an upside reversal in QQQ. Given the high-volume trading activity which is typically associated with the ETF, this is not particularly encouraging for tech stocks as a whole. But if we look at the contrarian trends present in the fund's latest inflow activity, it appears increasingly likely that tech stocks may be near a bottom after all of this recent selling pressure. This outlook is confirmed by the strong earnings results from core holdings like Apple and Amazon, so it would seem to be a matter of time before the market comes to its senses and resumes the broader uptrend visible in the technology space.
